why.Deuteronomy 28:68: The verse the whole movement rests on. Ships. Sold as slaves. A market so full that 'no man shall buy you.' Read it before you answer it.
why.Deuteronomy 17:16: Forbids the king to send the people back to Egypt. The ships in 28:68 are an exodus run backwards, answering this law.
why.Deuteronomy 29:1: Names who Moses is speaking to: covenant Israel, gathered at Moab. The one verse that fixes the chapter's audience.
why.Deuteronomy 30:1-10: The return promise, in the same covenant as the curses. Whoever the curses fall on, this chapter promises them home again.
why.Nehemiah 1:8-9: Nehemiah prays the return promise back to God by name. Evidence that Israel treated Deuteronomy 30 as a live clause, not a dead letter.
why.Galatians 3:13: 'Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law.' The suffering it describes was real. This verse says the curse itself has been carried.

why.2 Kings 17:7-23: Explains the Assyrian deportation of the northern kingdom as covenant judgment. The Bible narrating the curses landing, in its own words.
why.2 Chronicles 36:15-21: Does the same for Babylon: exile as the sanction the covenant named. A second report that the curses came.
why.Nehemiah 1:8-9: Nehemiah pleads the Deuteronomy 30 return clause by name. He treats the curse as spent and the promise as owed.
why.Nehemiah 9:32-37: A long public prayer owning the whole cycle. Sin, then kings, then exile, then serving foreign rulers. Israel telling its own story as judgment.
why.Daniel 9:11-13: 'The curse is poured upon us... that is written in the law of Moses.' Daniel says it happened, in his own lifetime.
why.Ezra 2:1-2: The register of families who came back from Babylon. It is also their best counter, since this list covers Judah and Benjamin only.
why.Lamentations 4:10: An eyewitness records mothers eating their own children in the siege. This is Deuteronomy 28:53-57, written by someone who watched it.

why.Deuteronomy 28:15: The 'if' the chapter hangs on. These curses follow breaking the covenant. They are tied to a covenant, not handed to whoever matches the list.
why.Ezra 2:59-63: Families were kept from the priesthood because they could not produce a genealogy. Israel settled identity by record, not by what a family had suffered.
why.Amos 9:7: God says he brought up the Philistines and Syrians too, as he brought Israel from Egypt. Being moved and afflicted by God does not make a people Israel.
why.Luke 13:1-5: Jesus is asked whether people who died badly were worse sinners. He says no, twice. Suffering does not tell you who someone is.

why.Numbers 1:18: At Israel's first census every man 'declared his pedigree' by family. Tribal membership was a written record from the start.
why.Ezra 2:62: Families who could not find their register were 'put from the priesthood.' Israel asked for documents, and refused claims made without them.
why.Genesis 49:1-28: Jacob's blessings on his twelve sons. The camps read modern nations off these portraits, so this is the chart's own proof text.
why.1 Timothy 1:4: Paul warns Timothy off 'endless genealogies' that breed questions rather than faith. Aimed at exactly this kind of chart-making.

why.Ezra 2:1-70: The full list of families returning from Babylon, counted by name. Judah's line is documented across the exile, with no gap to swap a people through.
why.Nehemiah 7:5-73: Nehemiah finds and copies the same register. A second witness that the returning families were named and kept.
why.Luke 2:36: Anna is 'of the tribe of Aser.' That is a northern tribe, seven hundred years after Assyria took them. Tribal identity was still known.
why.Romans 9:3-5: Paul calls the Jews of his own day 'my kinsmen according to the flesh' and 'Israelites.' He means the people in front of him.
why.Romans 11:1-5: Paul asks whether God cast off his people and says no. His proof is himself: 'I also am an Israelite, of the tribe of Benjamin.'
why.Revelation 2:9: 'Them which say they are Jews, and are not.' Their strongest text, and it deserves a real answer. Read the whole letter to Smyrna together.
why.Philippians 3:5: Paul names his own tribe — Benjamin — which is why the case can say the tribal records still existed in his lifetime.

why.Revelation 1:14-16: The description under dispute: hair white like wool, feet like burning brass. Note the eyes of flame and the sword in the same sentence.
why.Daniel 7:9: The Ancient of Days has hair 'like the pure wool.' Revelation is quoting Daniel, and nobody reads Daniel's figure as having a race.
why.Daniel 10:6: Arms and feet 'like in colour to polished brass,' written by a Hebrew. The source of the bronze image, used of a shining figure.
why.Isaiah 53:2: 'No beauty that we should desire him.' Read it to see how little Scripture cares how the Messiah looked.
why.Matthew 2:13-15: The flight into Egypt. The camps read it as a family who could pass unnoticed in Africa. A fair observation, and it settles nothing.
why.Exodus 2:19: Midianite women take Moses for an Egyptian. Real evidence that the Israelites did not look European. Concede it early and mean it.
why.Song of Solomon 1:5-6: 'I am black, but comely.' A Hebrew speaker describing herself. Another line worth granting rather than explaining away.

why.Revelation 2:9: 'Them which say they are Jews, and are not.' The heart of the impostor claim. It is a letter to one church in Smyrna, about a local fight.
why.Revelation 3:9: The same phrase again, in the letter to Philadelphia. Two cities, two local quarrels. That repetition marks a stock phrase, not a global prophecy.
why.Romans 11:1-2: 'God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.' Paul rules out the idea that Israel was quietly swapped for someone else.
why.Jeremiah 31:35-37: God stakes Israel's survival on the sun, moon and stars holding. Hard to square with a whole people vanishing and nobody noticing.
why.John 4:22: Jesus tells a Samaritan woman 'salvation is of the Jews,' meaning the Jews of his own day. He does not treat them as counterfeits.

why.Acts 17:26: God 'made of one blood all nations of men.' Worth saying out loud here, because this case can slide into ranking people by ancestry.
why.Exodus 12:38: A 'mixed multitude' left Egypt with Israel. Outsiders were in the nation from the first day. Israel was never a closed bloodline.
why.Ruth 1:16: A Moabite woman says 'thy people shall be my people.' She becomes David's great-grandmother. Covenant made her Israel, not descent.
why.Matthew 1:5: Rahab the Canaanite and Ruth the Moabite both stand in Jesus's family line. The genealogy itself argues against a pure bloodline.

why.Genesis 25:25: Esau born 'red, all over like an hairy garment.' The birth verse the whole doctrine is built on. Read it, then read 1 Samuel 16:12.
why.Genesis 25:30: Esau begs for the red stew and is named Edom. The name comes from that meal. It is not a description of a people.
why.1 Samuel 16:12: David is called admoni, the same Hebrew word used of Esau. The camps read David as Black. One word cannot carry two races.
why.1 Samuel 17:42: The word turns up again when Goliath looks at David. Two uses in one book, both of a ruddy young man rather than a race.
why.Deuteronomy 23:7: 'Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother.' The same covenant they quote, about the people they say is cursed.
why.Obadiah 1:10-14: Edom stands by while Jacob is plundered, and profits from it. This is the text behind their whole picture of a permanent enemy.
why.Obadiah 1:18: The house of Esau burned as stubble, read as the sentence on white people. Edom was a small kingdom in what is now southern Jordan.
why.Malachi 1:2-3: 'Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.' Their proof that the hostility is fixed by God rather than by history.
why.Romans 9:13: Paul quotes Malachi about God choosing. Three chapters later he says God's mercy reaches all. Read Romans 9 to 11 together or not at all.

why.Matthew 15:21-28: Their anchor text and its ending together. Jesus says he was sent only to Israel, then heals a Canaanite woman and praises her faith.
why.Acts 10:34-35: 'God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him is accepted.' Peter says it after God has corrected him.
why.Acts 10:44-48: The Spirit falls on a Roman household before anyone can baptise them. The decision is taken out of the church's hands.
why.Acts 15:7-11: The Jerusalem council rules that gentiles are saved the same way Jews are. The question was raised, argued and settled in writing.
why.Ephesians 2:11-19: The 'middle wall of partition' is broken down, and strangers become fellow citizens. The clearest statement that the boundary is gone.
why.Revelation 7:9: The redeemed are 'of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues.' From the book the camps quote most often.
why.Isaiah 49:6: Raising up the tribes of Jacob is called 'a light thing.' The servant is also 'a light to the Gentiles.' The Hebrew Bible says it first.
why.Matthew 28:19: 'Go ye therefore, and teach all nations.' The limited mission of Matthew 10 is replaced by this, at the end of the same book.

why.Romans 3:20-28: 'By the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified.' Paul's clearest line that law-keeping is not the ground of acceptance.
why.Galatians 2:16: 'A man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ.' The same point made three times in one verse.
why.Galatians 3:10-13: The heart of this case. Those under the law are 'under the curse,' and Christ redeemed them from it. Curse language, to a movement built on curses.
why.Deuteronomy 27:26: The verse Galatians 3:10 quotes. It opens the very curse chapter the movement uses as its identity document. Read both together.
why.Galatians 5:4: Whoever seeks to be justified by the law is 'fallen from grace.' Blunt, and it names what this case is actually about.
why.Acts 15:10-11: The apostles call the requirement a yoke 'which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear.' A Jewish council saying it about itself.
why.Ephesians 2:8-9: Saved by grace through faith, 'not of works.' Read verse 10 as well, which puts good works after salvation rather than under it.
why.Colossians 2:16-17: Names the exact practices at issue: food, drink, feast days and sabbaths. Paul calls them a shadow of what has come.

why.Galatians 3:7-9: 'They which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.' Paul answering the exact question the movement asks.
why.Galatians 3:26-29: 'If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.' Faith is the gate here, not descent.
why.Romans 2:28-29: Circumcision 'of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter.' Paul reopens who counts, without saying anyone is thrown out.
why.Romans 9:6-8: 'They are not all Israel, which are of Israel.' Written by a Jew about his own people, which is why it can be said at all.
why.Matthew 3:9: 'God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.' John shuts the door on any argument resting on ancestry alone.
why.John 8:37-44: Jesus tells men claiming Abraham as father that descent without Abraham's works proves nothing. Handle with care: this text has an ugly history of misuse.
why.Romans 11:1: 'Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.' Their strongest ground, and they are right about it. Grant it before you say anything else.
why.Jeremiah 31:35-37: Israel's permanence tied to the sun and moon. The anti-replacement text. Any Christian answer that erases Israel is contradicting this.
why.Romans 8:15-17: The Spirit of adoption, crying 'Abba, Father,' making believers joint-heirs. This is what the case is finally offering instead of a chart.
why.Galatians 4:4-7: Sonship comes by adoption, not by descent. This is the verse the bloodline argument has to answer.

why.Jeremiah 23:16: Warns of prophets who 'speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the LORD.' The founders' claims rest on visions.
why.Jude 1:3: 'The faith which was once delivered unto the saints.' Something once delivered has a source you can name. That is the question here.
why.Acts 17:11: The Bereans 'searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.' They are commended for checking. A chart deserves the same check.

why.Deuteronomy 18:20-22: The Torah's own test. If a prophet speaks and the thing does not happen, God did not say it. The movement applies this test to others.
why.Matthew 24:36: 'Of that day and hour knoweth no man.' Jesus rules out the whole business of naming a year.
why.Jeremiah 28:15-17: Hananiah predicts a date. Jeremiah tells him he will die that year, and he does. Scripture showing the test being used.
why.Matthew 24:23-26: Warns about people saying 'lo, here is Christ.' It matters because the leader who followed the failed date claimed to be the Holy Spirit.

why.Genesis 3:19: 'Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.' The plainest answer to a teaching that a renewed people would not die.
why.Hebrews 9:27: 'It is appointed unto men once to die.' One sentence, and it is the whole of what this case examines.
why.1 Corinthians 15:20-26: Death is 'the last enemy,' destroyed by resurrection. Scripture does promise the end of death, but not through diet or discipline.
why.1 Corinthians 15:53-57: The mortal 'must put on immortality.' The hope itself is real. It arrives by resurrection, and not before.
why.Deuteronomy 18:22: The test again. Ben Ammi made a claim you can check. Say what this community built before you check it.

why.Proverbs 18:17: 'He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.' Read the listing and the reply to it.
why.James 3:5-10: How much a small fire can burn. This is the point the critics have: what gets said on a street corner does not stay there.
why.1 Peter 3:15-16: Give your reason 'with meekness and fear.' The posture that stops a label doing the work an argument should do.

why.Judges 4:4-9: Deborah judges Israel and leads it into battle, with Barak refusing to go unless she comes. Scripture, not a modern reading.
why.2 Kings 22:14-20: Huldah the prophetess is asked to verify the rediscovered law book, while Jeremiah was alive. The king's own men went to her.
why.Acts 18:26: Priscilla is named before her husband. Together they take Apollos aside and teach him the way of God more exactly.
why.Romans 16:1-2: Phoebe is called a deacon and a patron, and Paul asks a whole church to help her. A woman carrying the letter and its weight.
why.Luke 24:1-11: Women are the first witnesses of the resurrection, in a world that did not accept a woman's testimony. God chose them anyway.
why.Ephesians 5:25-29: Headship defined as a husband giving himself up, to the point of death. That is the opposite of dominance, and it is the measure here.
why.1 Peter 3:7: Husband and wife are 'heirs together of the grace of life.' Equal standing, in a text the camps otherwise read closely.

why.Genesis 2:24: 'They shall be one flesh.' Two, not several. The verse Jesus goes back to when he is asked about marriage.
why.Matthew 19:4-6: Jesus is asked about marriage and answers from the beginning, quoting Genesis 2:24. He goes behind Moses, not around him.
why.Genesis 16:1-6: Abraham, Sarah and Hagar. The first plural household in Scripture, and it ends in contempt, harshness, and a woman fleeing into the desert.
why.Genesis 29:30-31: Jacob loves Rachel more than Leah, and God sees that Leah is hated. The rivalry runs through the rest of Genesis.
why.1 Samuel 1:6-7: Peninnah provokes Hannah year after year until she cannot eat. What the arrangement looked like from inside one home.
why.1 Kings 11:1-4: Solomon's many wives 'turned away his heart.' The one clear verdict Scripture passes on a household like this.
why.Deuteronomy 17:17: The king is told not to multiply wives. The Torah restraining the practice in the one office where power made it easy.
why.1 Corinthians 7:2-4: 'Let every man have his own wife, and every woman her own husband.' Paul writes as though the singular is simply assumed.
why.1 Timothy 3:2: An overseer must be 'the husband of one wife.' A pointless requirement if having several were simply good.
why.Titus 1:6: Paul requires an elder to be the husband of one wife — the New Testament line the case turns on.

why.Isaiah 28:7-13: Read the whole run, not verse 10. Drunken priests mock the prophet as baby-talk, and verse 13 turns their own taunt into the judgment.
why.2 Peter 1:20-21: 'No prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.' Both sides quote it, so read it with them rather than at them.
why.2 Peter 3:16: Warns that the unlearned 'wrest' hard passages to their own hurt. A New Testament name for the risk this case is about.
why.Nehemiah 8:8: The Levites read the book 'distinctly, and gave the sense.' Scripture's own picture of good reading: meaning, not word-chains.
why.Acts 17:11: The Bereans searched daily to check what they were told. Their defence uses this verse, and it is a fair use of it.
why.Luke 24:27: Jesus expounds himself 'from Moses and all the prophets.' They cite this for chain-reading. He was giving the sense, not matching words.

why.Isaiah 53:2: 'No beauty that we should desire him.' The only thing Scripture says about how he looked, and it is not a description.
why.1 Samuel 16:7: 'Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.' Said while choosing David. This verse ends the argument.
why.Revelation 1:14-16: The passage the fight is about. Handle it in its own case, calmly, beside Daniel 7. Never let it become the headline.
why.Acts 10:34-35: 'God is no respecter of persons.' The real question is who God accepts, and this answers it without mentioning anyone's looks.
why.2 Corinthians 5:16: 'Henceforth know we no man after the flesh.' Paul refusing to sort people by outward standing. Read it before this subject comes up.

why.Proverbs 18:13: 'He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.' That is what the blanket label does.
why.James 1:19: 'Swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.' The order matters. Ask which camp someone is in before deciding what they teach.
why.Titus 3:2: 'Speak evil of no man.' A false description of most of a movement is speaking evil, whatever the worst part of it does.
why.1 Peter 3:15-16: Answer 'with meekness and fear,' keeping a good conscience. The instruction assumes you have earned a hearing first.

why.Proverbs 18:17: The first account always sounds right until the other side speaks. A viral clip is a first account, cut by someone with a side.
why.Exodus 23:1-2: 'Thou shalt not raise a false report,' nor follow a crowd into wrong. Written for exactly this, three thousand years early.
why.Proverbs 14:15: 'The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.' The test to run on any clip before you use it.

why.Psalm 44:9-26: A whole psalm asking God why he has scattered and shamed his people. Scripture never rebukes the question. Neither should you.
why.Habakkuk 1:2-4: 'How long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear?' A prophet asking why God allows the violence he can see. The same question, in the Bible.
why.Isaiah 43:1: 'I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.' Speaks straight to the wound: a people whose names were taken from them.
why.Isaiah 56:3-8: God promises the outsider 'an everlasting name, better than of sons and daughters.' A name given by God, offered in the Hebrew Bible.
why.Hosea 1:10: Where it was said 'ye are not my people,' they shall be called 'the sons of the living God.' Belonging given, not proved.
why.Romans 8:15-17: The Spirit of adoption, crying 'Abba, Father.' Heirs, not applicants. This is what the whole section is trying to get to.
why.1 Peter 2:9-10: 'Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God.' The exact ache, answered without a genealogy.
why.John 1:12: 'To them gave he power to become the sons of God.' Sonship as a gift received, not a lineage you have to prove.
